title: POST {db}/read — the answer
description: The normalized form: every object once with its version, and the structure separately. Ids are relative to the database answering, and a reference into any other database is absolute. Type NAMES, never the catalog's integers.

objects.description: Every key is a bare id of the database answering. That is what stops a responder supplying objects for a database it does not own.

lists.description: Keyed `<frame>:<parent id>`. By frame and not by edge type: two aliases over one edge type with different filters or limits are two answers and must not collide.

counts.description: Keyed `<frame>:<parent id>`, then by the alias the count was asked for under. A count is separately authorized: an object may be readable while its count is not.

shape.description: Per frame, which alias leads to which frame. A consumer that does not hold the plan needs this to walk the lists, and a caller that chose the aliases uses it to map the responder's frame numbers back to its own.

ids.description: In order, after the filter and the limit. A member may be a REFERENCE: those are the ones this database did not follow, and they are how a read continues past it — the caller asks that database itself.

edges.description: The edge that reached each id, positionally. Absent where no edge did.

cursor.description: Where this list continues, to be handed back as a hop's `after`. Opaque: the responder dropped whatever its policy hides, so only the responder knows where the next page begins.
